summary: Forgotten Explorers is an interactive educational web prototype that turns discarded lunar and Martian space hardware into engaging first-person stories. Using real NASA open data, the platform connects students with historic landers, rovers, and probes left behind on the Moon and Mars, transforming silent scientific landmarks into interactive learning expeditions.
details:
The Challenge & Inspiration Decades of space exploration have left dozens of silent orbiters, landers, rovers, and scientific instruments across the Moon and Mars. While students often learn about dramatic rocket launches, they rarely get to know the machines that stayed behind on alien ground. We created Forgotten Explorers to give a voice to these robotic pioneers and turn space heritage into an accessible adventure.

How It Works Our web application acts as a "Space Heritage Diary" structured around a three-stage educational methodology: Discover, Understand, and Imagine. • Interactive Destinations (Moon & Mars): Users explore real mission archives, including the Ranger & Surveyor programs, the Apollo Lunar Surface legacy, and the Viking 1 & 2 Mars missions. • First-Person Storytelling: Each spacecraft features documented mission history told through an emotional, first-person diary perspective ("I was built to explore. I stayed to remember"), making engineering history relatable for young learners. • Decode the Science: Students inspect real hardware components (cameras, sensors, power cells) and coordinates to understand how each artifact functioned and what discoveries it unlocked.

Use of NASA Open Data Our prototype integrates real historical mission archives, surface imagery, landing coordinates, and telemetry records from NASA’s Open APIs, Public Data Catalog, and Mars Rover Photo Data to ensure scientific accuracy while fostering curiosity in future scientists.
